title: 1955 AHSME Problem 48
statement: Given triangle \(ABC\) with medians \(\overline{AE},\) \(\overline{BF},\) \(\overline{CD};\) \(\overline{FH}\) parallel and equal in length to \(\overline{AE};\) \(\overline{BH}\) and \(\overline{HE}\) are drawn; \(\overline{FE}\) extended meets \(\overline{BH}\) in \(G.\) Which one of the following statements is not necessarily correct?

solutions.text:
Set \(A=(0,0),\) \(B=(2,0),\) \(C=(u,v).\) Then \[ \begin{aligned} D&=(1,0),\\ E&=\left(\frac{u+2}{2},\frac v2\right),\\ F&=\left(\frac u2,\frac v2\right). \end{aligned} \] Since \(\overrightarrow{FH}=\overrightarrow{AE},\) we get \(H=(u+1,v).\) The horizontal line \(FE\) meets \(BH\) halfway from \(B\) to \(H,\) at \(G=(\frac{u+3}{2},\frac{v}{2}).\) These coordinates verify that \(AEHF\) is a parallelogram, \(\overrightarrow{BH}=\overrightarrow{DC},\) \(FG=\frac{3AB}{4},\) and \(G\) is the midpoint of \(BH,\) making \(FG\) a median. But \[ \begin{aligned} HE&=\frac12\sqrt{u^2+v^2},\\ HG&=\frac12\sqrt{(u-1)^2+v^2}, \end{aligned} \] which are not generally equal.

Thus, statement B is not necessarily correct.
hints: Use \(\overrightarrow{FH}=\overrightarrow{AE}\), then locate \(G\) where \(BH\) reaches height \(\frac{v}{2}\)
